note_text:
Patient is a 34-year-old woman referred for evaluation of possible allergic sensitization. She has been having intermittent episodes of nasal congestion, sneezing, and occasional urticarial rash over the past several months, with symptoms she describes as worse in certain settings. She has not kept a symptom diary correlating specific exposures to her episodes.

Vital signs stable. No acute distress noted on brief observation in clinic.

Plan: Order RAST panel for a broad set of environmental and food allergens (dust mite, cat, dog, ragweed, birch pollen, egg, milk, peanut, shellfish) to help narrow down possible triggers. Will review results at follow-up visit in 2-3 weeks. Patient advised to continue current antihistamine as needed.

No IgG/IgG subclass food antibody testing, ELISA/Act, LMRA, or qualitative multi-allergen screening ordered at this visit.
